verdict.rationale: Jules exposes an API that lets users script custom workflows and dispatch tasks programmatically (jules-docs-9, jules-docs-12), and usage-limit tiers explicitly target 'power users & agent-heavy workflows' with up to 300 tasks (jules-docs-13), while community reports confirm it 'handles large quantities of tasks very well' and users built custom dispatch tooling via the API/MCP bridge (jules-comm-11, jules-comm-19). However, there's no documented native UI or endpoint for a single bulk action across many items (e.g., batch-applying one task to many repos/issues) — each task still appears to be created and reviewed individually via GitHub labels or API calls. Missing for 10: a documented batch/bulk endpoint or UI feature, first-party bulk-operation examples, and independent verification of true parallel bulk execution rather than just high per-day task volume.
